name: Figma
tagline: Collaborative browser-based design and prototyping tool

pricing.notes: Official pricing/help checked 2026-07-30; Professional Full seat listed at $20/month monthly and $16/month annually.
pricing.freeTier: The free Starter plan gives limited access with unlimited drafts and daily AI credits.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 3 Figma Design/Sites files, 3 FigJam files and 3 Slides files per team; 3 pages per Starter team file; 30-day version history; 150 AI credits/day capped at 500/month.

tiers.name: Professional, Full seat
tiers.limits: 3,000 AI credits/month; unlimited team files and version history.

tiers.name: Professional, Dev seat
tiers.limits: 500 AI credits/month; Dev Mode access without full design editing.

tiers.name: Professional, Collab seat
tiers.limits: 500 AI credits/month; FigJam and Slides editing, but not full Figma Design editing.

tiers.name: Organization, Full seat
tiers.limits: 3,000 AI credits/month; organization-wide libraries and admin controls.

tiers.name: Enterprise, Full seat
tiers.limits: 3,000 AI credits/month; enterprise governance and workspaces.

tiers.name: Paid-plan View seat
tiers.limits: Unlimited viewers; 500 AI credits/month; view/comment/basic inspection only.
tiers.notes: Not a standalone plan; available inside paid organizations.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Starter: unlimited drafts, but each team gets 3 Design/Sites files, 3 FigJam files and 3 Slides files; 3 pages per team file; 30-day history; 150 AI credits/day up to 500/month.
pricing.billingTerms: Professional monthly + annual; Organization and Enterprise annual-only; AI credits reset monthly without rollover
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra AI credits require an add-on subscription or pay-as-you-go usage at prices not publicly listed. On a Professional annual plan, added seats can be charged separately at the full monthly rate until renewal; Organization/Enterprise additions are prorated and invoiced quarterly.

verdictSummary: You can make a small drawing/prototyping tool, but Figma's moat is real-time multiplayer editing, plugin ecosystem, design-system workflows, performance, and enterprise trust.
coreLoopDIY: Build a simple canvas editor with rectangles/text/components and export, but expect it to be a toy compared with Figma.
whatYouLose: your team, who are all on Figma
ten years of canvas performance engineering
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because entire product/design teams coordinate inside the file, not because drawing rectangles is hard.

priorArt.name: Penpot
priorArt.desc: open-source design tool; the serious alternative

alternatives.name: Lunacy
alternatives.desc: A polished free desktop UI editor with components, prototypes, cloud documents, and native apps; collaboration limits are small-team sized.

facts.install: Install a native Windows, macOS or Linux package, or open Lunacy in a browser
facts.engines: Icons8-hosted AI tools for background removal, upscaling, generated text and avatars; avatar generation integrates Generated Photos, while underlying model names are not disclosed
facts.dataFormat: Local designs are .sketch files on disk; cloud documents live on Icons8 servers and can be saved back as local .sketch files
facts.gapVsPaid: Its free cloud collaboration is small-team limited, and Figma's plugin ecosystem, browser collaboration and import fidelity remain stronger.

alternatives.name: Penpot
alternatives.desc: The real open-source answer: browser UI design, components, tokens, prototypes, comments, and multiplayer without pretending a whiteboard is Figma.

facts.install: Use the hosted signup, or download the official Docker Compose file and run docker compose up -d
facts.dataFormat: Hosted files in Penpot Cloud; self-hosted data in Docker volumes for PostgreSQL and uploaded assets, with exports based on SVG/CSS/HTML/JSON and open standards
facts.gapVsPaid: Its plugin ecosystem, Figma-file fidelity and hosted free-team/history limits are still behind Figma's mature collaborative platform.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker Compose, DNS and reverse-proxy/TLS knowledge; hosted signup has no setup blocker

alternatives.name: Quant-UX
alternatives.desc: Browser prototypes, collaboration, user tests, and analytics in one product; weaker than Figma for pixel-perfect design systems.

facts.install: Use the hosted Quant-UX signup, or run its multi-container Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: Hosted projects in Quant-UX's service; self-hosted prototypes and tests in MongoDB with uploaded images in mapped data directories
facts.gapVsPaid: It is primarily a prototyping and user-testing tool, not a production-grade vector editor and design-system workspace on Figma's level.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs several containers plus MongoDB, SMTP, a JWT secret, WebSocket URL and reverse-proxy/TLS configuration

rejectedAlternatives.name: Excalidraw
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent collaborative sketching, but hand-drawn boxes are not a component library, vector UI editor, or production design system.

rejectedAlternatives.name: OpenPencil
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Promising and properly open source, but its own README says it is under active development and not production-ready.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Pencil Project
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The classic recommendation is stale: the repository's last commit was January 2023, well outside the maintenance bar.

notes: The credibility entry. Figma's value is multiplayer CRDTs, a decade of canvas engineering, and everyone else being on it. You can't one-shot a moat; and network effects are the strongest moat there is.
prompt:
Build me a single-player vector canvas editor, a weekend sketch of Figma's core
canvas. Requirements:

- A canvas editor with rectangles, ellipses, text, and frames; select, move,
  and resize with handles; fill, stroke, and corner-radius controls in a right
  panel.
- A layers list with drag-reorder.
- Export the current selection as SVG and PNG.
- Local-first: documents persist to IndexedDB, with import and export as JSON.
- Vanilla JS or Svelte on a single canvas element, pick the simpler to ship; no
  backend at all.
- No accounts, no telemetry, everything stays in the browser on my machine.
- Out of scope: multiplayer, comments, components, auto-layout, and plugins.
  Do not build any collaboration or sync layer.
- README: state that this is not a Figma replacement, the moat is real-time
  multiplayer plus the network of people already on it, and point to Penpot or
  Excalidraw for serious single-player use.
